purpose: Track evidence strength behind high-use misconception records separately from diagnostic route coverage.

status_definitions.direct_empirical: A checked original study directly supports the relevant reasoning pattern within stated sample limits.
status_definitions.direct_empirical_language_mediated: A checked study directly supports the error pattern but shows that language structure materially affects whether/how it appears.
status_definitions.direct_empirical_broad_construct_or_mech: An original study supports the broader construct or mechanism, but not every detail of the MathBridge wording or target age range.
status_definitions.evidence_synthesis: An evidence-reviewed practice guide or research synthesis supports the instructional interpretation.
status_definitions.guidance_supported: Official/established teaching guidance or assessment response evidence supports use of the probe, while misconception-specific direct evidence remains narrower or unavailable.
status_definitions.curriculum_inferred: The pattern is mathematically plausible but direct evidence for the exact claim is not verified.
status_definitions.research_required: The exact wording is stronger than the evidence currently verified.

next_priority_records: all remaining misconception records not yet included in the evidence-depth audit
next_phase: Inventory every misconception record across base and extension catalogs and assign an explicit evidence class. This is an evidence-classification completeness task, not an attempt to claim every record has direct empirical prevalence evidence.
publication_rules: Never convert direct evidence from one population into a jurisdictional prevalence claim.
When evidence is language-mediated, retain the language scope explicitly.
A diagnostic item remains an instructional probe unless independently validated as an assessment instrument.
If evidence supports only a broader construct, teacher-facing text must use possible/may language.
A small qualitative or case-study sample can establish that a reasoning pattern occurs; it cannot establish population prevalence.
Guidance or assessment-response support is not equivalent to peer-reviewed misconception-specific evidence.
Evidence depth does not alter curriculum placement evidence.
